blocks.text: Have you ever wondered how businesses keep track of their transactions? The secret lies in source documents.

blocks.markdown: Source documents are the foundation of accounting records. They provide the evidence needed to record transactions accurately.

blocks.title: Definition of Source Documents
blocks.text: Source documents are original records that contain the details of a business transaction. They are used to verify and record financial data.

blocks.markdown: Common source documents include invoices, receipts, credit notes, and debit notes. Each serves a specific purpose in the accounting process.

items: Invoice: A document issued by a seller to a buyer, indicating the products, quantities, and agreed prices for products or services.
Receipt: A document acknowledging that payment has been received.
Credit Note: A document issued to a buyer, reducing the amount owed due to a return of goods or an allowance.
Debit Note: A document sent by a buyer to a seller, indicating a return of goods or a request for a reduction in the amount owed.

blocks.title: Tracing a Source Document
blocks.prompt: How would you record a transaction using an invoice?

steps.text: Identify the invoice from the transaction.
Record the details in the Sales Journal as it indicates a sale.
Post the transaction to the appropriate ledger accounts.

blocks.answer: The invoice is recorded in the Sales Journal, and the transaction is posted to the sales and accounts receivable ledgers.

blocks.markdown: Understanding the differences between these documents is crucial for accurate bookkeeping and financial reporting.

blocks.title: Exam Tip
blocks.text: Always check the details on a source document to ensure accuracy before recording it in the books of original entry.

points: Source documents are essential for verifying and recording transactions.
Invoices, receipts, credit notes, and debit notes each have specific roles in accounting.
